questions.question:
D1 — Reduce the pricing-tier plan to a minimal version, or proceed with all four components as written?
Project/branch/task: main branch, reviewing plan.md ("developer-friendly" pricing tier).
ELI10: The plan builds four new things (Stripe tier, pricing page, entitlements table, Redis cache) to test a hunch that developers find us too expensive. Nobody has asked a developer yet. If the hunch is wrong, all four pieces are wasted and we now maintain a cache and a table nobody needed. If the hunch is right, a single Stripe price plus a feature-flagged page proves it just as well.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Over-build and we carry Redis plus an extra table forever for a tier that may not move signups. Under-build and we ship a tier we can't measure or roll back.
Recommendation: A because the goal is learning whether price is the barrier, and a Stripe price + flagged page + one column answers that with the least surface area to secure, test, and roll back.
Completeness: A=9/10, B=7/10, C=5/10 (C has more parts but ships with no tests, no auth check, no rollout, so it covers less of what matters)
Pros / cons:
A) Minimal: validate premise, Stripe price, flagged pricing page, plan column, no Redis (recommended) (human: ~1 week incl. 5-8 developer conversations / CC: ~30 min build, interviews stay human-bound)
  ✅ Smallest blast radius: one Stripe price, one column, one flag, easy to roll back or delete if the hunch is wrong
  ✅ Forces a real success metric (developer signups vs. baseline over N weeks) before code is written
  ✅ Frees room in this PR for the missing tests, auth check on upgrade, and a rollout plan
  ❌ Slower to a shipped tier because talking to developers first takes calendar time
B) Middle: Stripe tier + pricing page + entitlements table, drop Redis, add tests/auth/rollout (human: ~2 weeks / CC: ~1 hr)
  ✅ Keeps a dedicated entitlements table if you already know more tiers or per-customer overrides are coming
  ✅ Drops the one component (Redis) with no stated justification while keeping the rest of the team's intent
  ❌ Still builds a schema abstraction for a single tier before the premise is validated
C) Proceed as-is: all four components including Redis (human: ~3-4 weeks / CC: ~2 hr)
  ✅ Matches what the team already agreed to, no re-litigating the design internally
  ✅ Redis is in place if entitlement reads ever become a measured hot path
  ❌ Adds a cache and a table for an unobserved performance problem, and the plan currently has no tests, no auth on upgrade, and no rollout path
Net: You're trading a few days of developer conversations and a smaller diff against carrying two pieces of infrastructure for a hypothesis nobody has tested.
